name: Boulder Daily Camera editorial board
lean_basis: Boulder's daily newspaper. No independent media-bias rating was captured. Its 2026 local picks split: NO on the city bond (2K), debt-limit change (2M) and vacancy tax (2J); YES on the county child care tax (1A), firefighter bargaining (2L) and a bigger county commission (200). Its candidate endorsements, if any, were not captured.

name: League of Women Voters of Boulder County
lean_basis: Nonpartisan civic organization. Takes measure positions based on its adopted local, state and national League positions (critics on the right call those left-leaning) and may stay neutral; never endorses candidates. In 2026 it supported 1A, 200, 2K and 2M, picked option 2 on 201, and was neutral on 2J and 2L.

name: Boulder Reporting Lab
lean_basis: Local nonprofit newsroom. Publishes candidate profiles and questionnaires (including how each city candidate says they'd vote on the seven local measures); no endorsements were found. Its questionnaire answers appear in candidates' own words, not as endorsements.

name: PLAN-Boulder County
lean_basis: Self-described citizen-led advocacy group founded in 1959; historically focused on open space and environmental protection (Boulder Reporting Lab). In Boulder's nonpartisan city politics it is usually on the slower-growth side, often opposite Boulder Progressives. Its 2026 mayoral picks cross Boulder's factions (La Grave first, Adams second). 'Lean left' reflects its environmental platform; it is not a party group and the national left-right scale fits Boulder's local divides poorly.

name: Better Boulder
lean_basis: Local 501(c)(6) group that endorses city candidates and measures (per its own podcast). Six of its eight 2026 city picks overlap with Boulder Progressives' slate; the other two (Winer, Jamieson) are also PLAN-Boulder or Open Boulder picks. No self-described or third-party national lean found; 'lean left' is an approximation within Boulder's Democratic-leaning politics.

name: Boulder Progressives
lean_basis: Boulder Reporting Lab describes it as 'a progressive political organization.' Endorses in Boulder's nonpartisan city races. Its 2026 picks are taken from Boulder Reporting Lab's candidate listing; its own announcement page was not opened.

name: Open Boulder
lean_basis: Boulder Reporting Lab describes it as associated with Boulder's 'more moderate bloc.' No national-party lean found; 'lean left' is an approximation for the moderate end of Boulder's Democratic-leaning politics. Picks taken from Boulder Reporting Lab's candidate listing; Open Boulder's own page was not captured.

name: Boulder Democratic Socialists of America
lean_basis: Local chapter of a self-described democratic socialist organization. Picks taken from Boulder Reporting Lab's candidate listing; the chapter's own page was not captured.

name: Colorado Working Families Party
lean_basis: Self-described progressive, multiracial, feminist populist party; endorses mostly Democrats to the left of the party mainstream. Boulder picks taken from Boulder Reporting Lab's candidate listing.

name: Boulder Area Labor Council
lean_basis: Regional federation of labor unions. Like the Denver Area Labor Federation and Colorado AFL-CIO elsewhere in this guide, labor federations here back Democrats in partisan races; in Boulder's nonpartisan council race it backed three candidates also endorsed by Boulder Progressives. Picks taken from Boulder Reporting Lab's candidate listing; the council's own 2026 slate was not found.

name: Boulder County Board of Commissioners (official board positions)
lean_basis: Elected partisan board. Commissioner Ashley Stolzmann is on the 2026 ballot as a Democrat, and all three commissioners endorsed candidates in the June 2026 Democratic CU Regent primary (Boulder Reporting Lab). On every 2026 measure where both took a stand, the board's position matches the Boulder County Democratic Party's. This is a government body's official position, not a campaign endorsement.
